newsitem.title: UK: Mars bar sets new UK ad as part of 9mln stg budget.
newsitem.headline: Mars bar sets new UK ad as part of 9mln stg budget.

text.p: The Mars candy bar, that chewy confection of chocolate and caramel, will launch a new television advertising campaign in Britain on Sunday, as part of a doubling in its UK advertising budget.
"We are starting a new advertising campaign on Sunday," Rachel Bradley, UK brand manager for Mars, told Reuters on Thursday in a telephone interview.
"We will be spending nine million pounds ($15.2 million) on advertising the Mars brand this year," she said. "It's effectively doubling what we spent in 1996.
"In a market as mature as the confectionery market, advertising is one of the best ways of talking to our customers," Bradley said.
The new ad features an old Native American man climbing a mountain with his son. The man says: "Son, this is a good day to die."

The man lies down exhausted at the top of the mountain, and as the son reaches to cover him with a blanket, a Mars bar falls from his pocket. The old man eats the Mars bar, and a voice-over says: "There is nothing like the great taste of Mars -- it's the taste for life."

The ad, created by the DMB&B ad agency, has been shown in other markets in continental Europe, but has never been shown before in Britain. It has not been shown in the U.S., where privately-held Mars has its headquarters.
The ad is a departure from the sports-oriented ads that Mars last ran but Bradley said it is consistent with the message that Mars has always conveyed.
"The message about Mars giving you the energy to carry on with life and helping you have a positive approach to life is the message we've always had," Bradley added.

She said the move away from sports images did not signal an effort to make the confection more appealing to women. "The Mars bar has always appealed to women," she said. "Certainly this is a different way of saying the same thing in a different way."
Bradley said it has not yet decided if the planned nine million pound advertising budget for 1996 will include other ads in addition to the one being unveiled on Sunday.
